title: Comparing fractions
summary: Compare fractions using equal parts, same whole, and a fraction bar.

teach.md: Fractions name a share of the **same whole**. Compare the shaded lengths — the bars do the work.

frames.caption: Same whole, different shaded amounts.
Same-size twelfths: nine shaded beats eight.
The larger share sits farther right on the number line.

frames.alt: Reference: proper fractions placed on number lines (CC BY-SA 4.0).
frames.caption: Curated number-line reference for fraction magnitude.

misconceptions.note_md: A bigger denominator means smaller parts. Compare the shaded amounts instead.

probe.explain_md: 3/4 and 2/3 share the same whole, and 3/4 shades more of it, so 3/4 is bigger.

explain_frames.caption: 3/4 is farther right on the number line.

probe.solution_md: Use a common denominator of 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12, so 3/4 is bigger.
probe.hint_md: Line up the two bars and compare the shaded lengths.

misconceptions.note_md: A bigger denominator means smaller parts. Compare the shaded amounts instead.

probe.explain_md: 2/3 and 1/2 share the same whole, and 2/3 shades more of it, so 2/3 is bigger.

explain_frames.caption: 2/3 is farther right on the number line.

probe.solution_md: Use a common denominator of 6: 2/3 = 4/6 and 1/2 = 3/6, so 2/3 is bigger.
probe.hint_md: Line up the two bars and compare the shaded lengths.

misconceptions.note_md: A bigger denominator means smaller parts. Compare the shaded amounts instead.

probe.explain_md: 3/5 and 2/4 share the same whole, and 3/5 shades more of it, so 3/5 is bigger.

explain_frames.caption: 3/5 is farther right on the number line.

probe.solution_md: Use decimals: 3/5 = 0.6 and 2/4 = 0.5, so 3/5 is bigger.
probe.hint_md: Line up the two bars and compare the shaded lengths.

worked_example.md: Rewrite both with twelfths: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12. Nine twelfths is more than eight, so 3/4 is bigger.

frames.caption: Common denominator 12.

worked_example_alt.md: On the number line, 3/4 is farther right than 2/3. Farther right means bigger.

frames.caption: Number-line check.

teach.md: The **denominator** is the bottom number. It counts how many **equal** parts the whole is cut into — every slice the same size.

frames.caption: Count every equal slice of the whole.
Six equal parts make the whole.
